title: Tits Cones, Chambers, and Parabolic Stabilizers

items.title: The Tits cone, its interior, and the negative-root set of a functional
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set, $m$ a Coxeter matrix on $S$, $W$ the presented group with length function $\ell$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), $V=\mathbb R^S$ with Coxeter form $B$ and reflections $r_a$ ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]]), $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ the canonical reflection homomorphism with root system $\Phi$ and positive cone $V_+$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]]), and let $V^*$ be the algebraic dual with its dual action, closed chamber $C$, faces $C_I$ and root hyperplanes $H_\alpha$ in the notation of [[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]]. Let $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup\Phi_-$ be the signed root system and $C^\circ=\bigcap_{s\in S}\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)>0\}$ the open chamber ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]]).

**(1) The chamber system.** For $w\in W$ put $wC:=\{w\cdot f:f\in C\}$. The sets $wC$ are the **chambers** of $(W,S)$ and $C$ is the **fundamental chamber**; for $w\in W$ and $s\in S$ the hyperplane $wH_{e_s}$ is a **wall** of the chamber $wC$.

**(2) The Tits cone.** The **Tits cone** is
$$U:=\bigcup_{w\in W}wC\subseteq V^*.$$
This definition asserts no convexity or closedness of $U$, face-intersection properties, or local finiteness. Convexity is proved in [[thm-cg-tits-cone-finite-negativity-and-convexity]], chamber intersections in [[thm-cg-dual-chamber-intersections-and-point-stabilizers]], and local finiteness of chambers and walls only at points of $U^\circ$ in [[thm-cg-tits-cone-interior-and-local-finiteness]] (3). Immediate from the definition, the group law and the left-action property of the dual action ([[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]] (1)): $C\subseteq U$, $0\in U$ (because $0\in C$), and $w'U=U$ for every $w'\in W$.

**(3) The finite-dimensional topology and the interior.** Since $S$ is finite, $f\mapsto(f(e_s))_{s\in S}$ is a linear bijection $V^*\to\mathbb R^S$ ([[def-dual-family-associated-to-a-basis]], [[thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension]], [[def-linear-basis]]). If $S\ne\emptyset$, pulling back the metric $d_\infty$ of [[lem-metrics-on-rn]] along this bijection gives the metric
$$d(f,g):=\max_{s\in S}|f(e_s)-g(e_s)|$$
on $V^*$ ([[def-metric-space]], [[def-metric-topology]]); if $S=\emptyset$ then $V^*=\{0\}$ is a singleton and $d$ is its unique metric, $d(0,0)=0$.

A second basis enters only when $S\ne\emptyset$. If $(e'_t)$ is a second basis with $e'_t=\sum_{s\in S}a_{ts}e_s$, then $\max_t|f(e'_t)|\le C\max_s|f(e_s)|$ and $\max_s|f(e_s)|\le C'\max_t|f(e'_t)|$ with $C=\max_t\sum_s|a_{ts}|$ and $C'$ the analogous constant of the inverse matrix, whose entries are finite because $S$ is finite; so a second coordinate system gives an equivalent norm, hence the same open sets and the same interior ([[thm-all-norms-on-rn-are-equivalent]]). The **interior of the Tits cone** is
$$U^\circ:=\operatorname{int}U,$$
the interior of $U$ for this ordinary finite-dimensional topology ([[def-metric-interior-closure-boundary]]). Thus a **neighborhood** of $f$ is a set containing some ball $\{g:d(f,g)<\varepsilon\}$, $\varepsilon>0$, and **compact** means compact for this topology ([[def-metric-compactness]]).

**(4) The negative-root set of a functional.** For $f\in V^*$ put
$$\operatorname{Neg}(f):=\{\alpha\in\Phi_+:f(\alpha)<0\}\subseteq\Phi_+.$$
This attaches a set of positive roots to a functional; it is not the inversion set $N(w)$ attached to a group element ([[def-cg-geometric-inversion-set]]). No finiteness of $\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ is asserted by this definition: the equivalence "$f\in U$ if and only if $\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ is finite" is the theorem [[thm-cg-tits-cone-finite-negativity-and-convexity]].
items.strategy: A definition item. The chamber system and the union $U$ are set-theoretic definitions built from the dual action of [[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]]; the metric is the pullback of $d_\infty$ along the coordinate bijection $f\mapsto(f(e_s))_s$, and the independence of the topology from the chosen basis is the explicit two-sided bound by the change-of-coordinate matrix and its inverse (its entries are finite because $S$ is finite). The qualifications in (2) and (4) are part of the definition: convexity and chamber intersections are deferred to the named theorems, local finiteness of chambers and walls is deferred only at points of $U^\circ$, no general closedness claim is made, and the negative-root set carries no finiteness assertion. The dual action, the chamber $C$, its faces and the hyperplanes $H_\alpha$ are imported from the previous pair rather than redefined, and the signed root system from [[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]]. No Choice is used: $S$ is finite and all constructions are finite-dimensional or set-theoretic.

items.title: The finite-negativity criterion, the reduction step, and convexity of the Tits cone
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $W$, $\ell$, $V$, $B$, $\rho$, $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup\Phi_-$, $V_+$, $C$, $C^\circ$, the chambers $wC$, the Tits cone $U$ and the negative-root sets $\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ be as in [[def-cg-tits-cone-and-fundamental-chamber]].

**(1) Finite-negativity criterion.** For every $f\in V^*$,
$$f\in U\iff\operatorname{Neg}(f)\ \text{is finite}.$$

**(2) The chamber as the empty negative-root set.** For every $f\in V^*$, $\operatorname{Neg}(f)=\emptyset$ if and only if $f\in C$.

**(3) Reduction step.** Let $f\in V^*$ with $\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ finite and $f\notin C$, and let $s\in S$ with $f(e_s)<0$ (such an $s$ exists). Then $e_s\in\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ and
$$\operatorname{Neg}(s\cdot f)=r_s\bigl(\operatorname{Neg}(f)\setminus\{e_s\}\bigr),\qquad |\operatorname{Neg}(s\cdot f)|=|\operatorname{Neg}(f)|-1.$$
Iterating, after exactly $|\operatorname{Neg}(f)|$ steps one reaches an element $w\in W$ with $w\cdot f\in C$.

**(4) Convexity.** $U$ is closed under nonnegative scalar multiples and under convex combinations:
$$f\in U,\ \lambda\ge0\ \Longrightarrow\ \lambda f\in U;\qquad f,g\in U,\ t\in[0,1]\ \Longrightarrow\ (1-t)f+tg\in U .$$

**(5) Inversion-set bounds.** If $f\in U$ and $w\in W$ satisfies $w\cdot f\in C$, then
$$\operatorname{Neg}(f)\subseteq N(w)\qquad\text{and}\qquad |\operatorname{Neg}(f)|\le\ell(w).$$
items.strategy:
**(1) and (5), direction $f\in U\Rightarrow\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ finite.** Write $f=w\cdot g$ with $g\in C$. A functional of $C$ is nonnegative on the positive cone: $g(e_s)\ge0$ for all $s$ and $V_+$ is the cone generated by the $e_s$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]] (3)), so $g$ is nonnegative on $V_+$; and $\Phi_+\subseteq V_+\setminus\{0\}$ ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2)). Hence for $\alpha\in\operatorname{Neg}(f)$, i.e. $\alpha\in\Phi_+$ with $g(\rho(w)^{-1}\alpha)=f(\alpha)<0$, the root $\rho(w)^{-1}\alpha$ lies in $\Phi_-$, so $\alpha\in N(w^{-1})$ ([[def-cg-geometric-inversion-set]] (1)). This gives (5) together with $|N(w^{-1})|=\ell(w^{-1})$ ([[thm-cg-root-inversion-formulas-and-strong-exchange]] (2)); and $\ell(w^{-1})=\ell(w)$ because reversing a reduced expression of $w$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]) is a reduced expression of $w^{-1}$ and vice versa. So $\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ is finite.
**Direction $\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ finite $\Rightarrow f\in U$, and (2), (3).** Suppose first $\operatorname{Neg}(f)=\emptyset$; then $f(e_s)\ge0$ for every $s$, since $e_s\in\Phi_+$ ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2)), so $f\in C$; conversely $f\in C$ gives $f(\alpha)\ge0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi_+$ because $\alpha$ is a nonnegative combination of the $e_s$ and $f$ is linear, so $\operatorname{Neg}(f)=\emptyset$; this is (2). Now let $N:=\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ be finite and nonempty and induct on $n:=|N|$ ([[def-finite-cardinality]], [[thm-induction-principle]]). Since $N\subseteq V_+\setminus\{0\}$, an element $\alpha=\sum_sc_se_s$ of $N$ has some coefficient $c_s>0$; then $f(\alpha)=\sum_sc_sf(e_s)<0$ forces $f(e_s)<0$ for that $s$, so $s$ as required exists and $e_s\in N$ ($e_s\in\Phi_+$). For every $\beta\in\Phi_+$, $(s\cdot f)(\beta)=f(r_s\beta)$ by the definition of the dual action ([[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]] (1)), and by the reflection formula $r_s\beta=\beta-2B(\beta,e_s)e_s$ ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] (3), [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] (2)). For $\beta=e_s$ this gives $(s\cdot f)(e_s)=f(-e_s)=-f(e_s)>0$. For $\beta\ne e_s$ the simple reflection permutes $\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\}$ and is an involution there ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (3)), so $\beta\in\operatorname{Neg}(s\cdot f)$ if and only if $r_s\beta\in N\setminus\{e_s\}$, i.e. $\operatorname{Neg}(s\cdot f)=r_s(N\setminus\{e_s\})$, of cardinality $n-1$. By the induction hypothesis $s\cdot f\in U$, say $s\cdot f=u\cdot g$ with $g\in C$; then $f=s\cdot(s\cdot f)\in U$ because $U$ is $W$-invariant by [[def-cg-tits-cone-and-fundamental-chamber]] (2). The induction also runs the reduction step downwards, giving (3).
**(4)** By linearity, $\operatorname{Neg}(\lambda f)=\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ for $\lambda>0$ and $\operatorname{Neg}(0)=\emptyset$; and $\operatorname{Neg}((1-t)f+tg)\subseteq\operatorname{Neg}(f)\cup\operatorname{Neg}(g)$ for $t\in[0,1]$, since $(1-t)f(\alpha)+tg(\alpha)<0$ forces $f(\alpha)<0$ or $g(\alpha)<0$. The criterion (1) therefore gives closure under nonnegative scalings and convex combinations, endpoints $t=0,1$ included. No Choice is used: the induction is on the natural number $|N|$, and all statements are evaluated at finitely many coordinates.
items.proof_strategy: direct computation and induction on the size of the negative-root set

items.title: Chamber collisions, point stabilizers, and the intersection rule
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $W$, $\ell$, $V$, $B$, $\rho$, $\Phi$, $C$, $C^\circ$, the chambers $wC$ and the Tits cone $U$ be as in [[def-cg-tits-cone-and-fundamental-chamber]]; for $I\subseteq S$ put $W_I:=\langle s:s\in I\rangle$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]) and for $f\in V^*$ put $S(f):=\{s\in S:f(e_s)=0\}$.

**(1) Walls are root hyperplanes.** For all $w\in W$ and $s\in S$,
$$wH_{e_s}=H_{\rho(w)e_s};$$
hence the walls of the chamber system are exactly the root hyperplanes $H_\alpha$, $\alpha\in\Phi$.

**(2) Side rule.** For all $w\in W$ and $s\in S$,
$$wC^\circ\subseteq\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)>0\}\iff\ell(sw)>\ell(w),\qquad wC^\circ\subseteq\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)<0\}\iff\ell(sw)<\ell(w),$$
and exactly one of the two alternatives holds. If $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$ then $C\subseteq\{f:f(e_s)\ge0\}$ and $wC\subseteq\{f:f(e_s)\le0\}$: the chambers $C$ and $wC$ lie on opposite sides of the wall $H_{e_s}$.

**(3) Collision.** If $f,g\in C$, $w\in W$ and $w\cdot f=g$, then $f=g$ and $w\in W_{S(f)}$.

**(4) Point stabilizers.** For every $f\in C$, $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=W_{S(f)}$. For $f\in U$ and $w\in W$ with $w^{-1}\cdot f\in C$ one has
$$\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=w\,W_{S(w^{-1}\cdot f)}\,w^{-1}.$$

**(5) The intersection rule.** For every $w\in W$, with $\overline C_T:=\{f\in C:f(e_s)=0\text{ for all }s\in T\}$,
$$wC\cap C=\{f\in C:w\in W_{S(f)}\}=\bigcup_{\substack{T\subseteq S\\ w\in W_T}}\overline C_T .$$

**(6) Strict fundamental domain.** Every $W$-orbit contained in $U$ meets $C$ in exactly one point. In particular the open chambers $wC^\circ$ ($w\in W$) are pairwise disjoint, and the chambers meeting in a face are described by (5).
items.strategy:
**(1)** Unfold the dual action: $f\in wH_{e_s}$ means $(w^{-1}\cdot f)(e_s)=0$, and $(w^{-1}\cdot f)(e_s)=f(\rho(w)e_s)$ ([[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]] (1)), which is exactly $f\in H_{\rho(w)e_s}$. Every wall of a chamber is such a translate and $\{\rho(w)e_s:w\in W,s\in S\}=\Phi$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]] (2)), giving the second sentence.
**(2)** Fix $x\in C^\circ$ and put $\beta:=\rho(w)^{-1}e_s=\rho(w^{-1})e_s$. By the signed root system, $\beta\in\Phi_+$ or $\beta\in\Phi_-$ ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2)), and by the root-length criterion ([[thm-cg-root-length-criterion-and-faithfulness]] (1)) applied to $w^{-1}$, $\beta\in\Phi_+$ if and only if $\ell(w^{-1}s)>\ell(w^{-1})$, that is, $\ell(sw)>\ell(w)$ (length is inversion-invariant; reverse reduced expressions). A functional of the open chamber is positive on $\Phi_+\setminus\{0\}$ and negative on $\Phi_-$: for $\gamma=\sum_sc_se_s\in V_+\setminus\{0\}$ some $c_s>0$ and $x(\gamma)=\sum_sc_sx(e_s)>0$. Hence $(w\cdot x)(e_s)=x(\beta)$ is positive, respectively negative, exactly as the displayed equivalence says, and this sign is the same for every $x\in C^\circ$. Parity $\ell(sw)=\ell(w)\pm1$ ([[thm-hh-coxeter-exchange-deletion-and-faithfulness]] (1)) makes the two alternatives exclusive. If $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$ and $x\in C$ (not necessarily open), write $\beta=-b$ with $b\in\Phi_+\setminus\{0\}$; then $(w\cdot x)(e_s)=x(\beta)=-x(b)\le0$, since $x$ is nonnegative on the cone $V_+$ and $\Phi_+\subseteq V_+$. Thus $wC\subseteq\{f:f(e_s)\le0\}$, while $C\subseteq\{f:f(e_s)\ge0\}$ by definition.
**(3)** Induct on $k:=\ell(w)$. For $w=1$ we have $f=g$ and $1\in W_{S(f)}$. If $k\ge1$, a reduced expression of $w$ begins with some $s\in S$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), and then $\ell(sw)=k-1$ by the exchange property ([[thm-hh-coxeter-exchange-deletion-and-faithfulness]] (2)); write $w=sw'$ with $\ell(w')=k-1$. By (2), $wC\subseteq\{f:f(e_s)\le0\}$ and $C\subseteq\{f:f(e_s)\ge0\}$, and $g=w\cdot f$ lies in both, so $g(e_s)=0$. Then $s\cdot g=g$: for $t\ne s$, $(s\cdot g)(e_t)=g(r_se_t)=g(e_t+2c(s,t)e_s)=g(e_t)$ by the reflection formula ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] (3), [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]]), while $(s\cdot g)(e_s)=g(-e_s)=0=g(e_s)$; two linear functionals agreeing on the basis $(e_t)$ of $V$ ([[def-linear-basis]]) are equal. Hence $g=s\cdot g=s\cdot(w\cdot f)=(sw)\cdot f=w'\cdot f$, and the induction hypothesis applied to $w'$ and the pair $(f,g)$ gives $f=g$ and $w'\in W_{S(f)}$. Since $g(e_s)=0$ and $f=g$, we have $s\in S(f)$; so $w=sw'\in W_{S(f)}$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]).
**(4)** If $f\in C$ and $s\in S(f)$, the same basis computation as in (3) gives $s\cdot f=f$; hence every element of the subgroup $W_{S(f)}$ generated by these $s$ fixes $f$. Conversely, $w\cdot f=f$ with $f\in C$ is the case $g=f$ of (3), so $w\in W_{S(f)}$. For the second formula, $\operatorname{Stab}_W(w\cdot g)=w\operatorname{Stab}_W(g)w^{-1}$ for every $g$ (conjugation in $W$), and $w^{-1}\cdot f\in C$ has stabilizer $W_{S(w^{-1}\cdot f)}$ by the first formula.
**(5)** If $f\in C$ and $w\in W_T$ for some $T\subseteq S(f)$, then $w\in W_{S(f)}$ and $w\cdot f=f$ by (4), so $f\in wC\cap C$ and $f\in\overline C_T$. Conversely, if $f\in wC\cap C$ then $w^{-1}\cdot f\in C$ and $f\in C$, so (3) applied to the element $w^{-1}$ and the pair $(f,w^{-1}\cdot f)$ gives $f=w^{-1}\cdot f$ and $w^{-1}\in W_{S(f)}$; then $w\in W_{S(f)}$, and $f$ lies in $\overline C_T$ for $T:=S(f)$. This proves both descriptions of $wC\cap C$.
**(6)** Every $f\in U$ lies in some $wC$ with $w\in W$, so its orbit meets $C$. If $x,y\in C$ lie in the same $W$-orbit, say $y=w\cdot x$, then (3) gives $x=y$; this is uniqueness. For the disjointness of open chambers, if $z\in wC^\circ\cap vC^\circ$ then $w^{-1}\cdot z,v^{-1}\cdot z\in C^\circ$ lie in one orbit, hence are equal by uniqueness, and $(v^{-1}w)\cdot(w^{-1}\cdot z)=v^{-1}\cdot z$ with $w^{-1}\cdot z\in C^\circ$; (3) with $f=w^{-1}\cdot z$ and $g=v^{-1}\cdot z$ gives $w^{-1}\cdot z=v^{-1}\cdot z$ and $v^{-1}w\in W_{S(w^{-1}\cdot z)}=W_\emptyset=\{1\}$ (the interior point has $S=\emptyset$, and $\langle\emptyset\rangle=\{1\}$). So $w=v$; this recovers [[thm-cg-root-length-criterion-and-faithfulness]] (2). No Choice is used.

items.title: The interior of the Tits cone, finite parabolic stabilizers, and local finiteness
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $W$, $\ell$, $V$, $B$, $\rho$, $\Phi$, $C$, $C^\circ$, the faces $C_I$, the chambers $wC$, the walls, the Tits cone $U$, its interior $U^\circ$ and $\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ be as in [[def-cg-tits-cone-and-fundamental-chamber]] and [[thm-cg-dual-chamber-intersections-and-point-stabilizers]]; for $I\subseteq S$ put $W_I=\langle s:s\in I\rangle$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]) and $\overline C_I=\{f\in C:f(e_s)=0\text{ for all }s\in I\}$.

**(1) Interior criterion.** Let $f\in C$ and $I:=S(f)=\{s\in S:f(e_s)=0\}$. Then
$$f\in U^\circ\iff W_I\ \text{is finite}.$$

**(2) The interior is the union of the spherical faces.** $U^\circ$ is $W$-invariant, and with $C^f:=\bigcup\{C_I:I\subseteq S,\ W_I\ \text{finite}\}=\{f\in C:W_{S(f)}\ \text{finite}\}$,
$$U^\circ=\bigcup_{w\in W}w\cdot C^f .$$

**(3) Local finiteness.** Let $f\in U^\circ$, write $f=w\cdot f_0$ with $f_0\in C$ and put $I:=S(f_0)$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that
(i) $\{g:d(f,g)<\varepsilon\}\subseteq\bigcup_{u\in W_I}w\,uC$;
(ii) every chamber meeting $\{g:d(f,g)<\varepsilon\}$ is one of the chambers $w\,uC$, $u\in W_I$;
(iii) every wall meeting $\{g:d(f,g)<\varepsilon\}$ is one of the walls $w\,uH_{e_s}$, $u\in W_I$, $s\in S$.
Consequently every point of $U^\circ$ has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many chambers and only finitely many walls, and every compact subset of $U^\circ$ is met by only finitely many chambers and only finitely many walls.

**(4) Boundary.** Let $f\in C$ with $W_{S(f)}$ infinite, and put $I:=S(f)$. Then $f\notin U^\circ$; more precisely, with $f_s\in V^*$ the dual basis functionals of $(e_s)$ and $\delta_I:=\sum_{s\in I}f_s$:
(i) $f-t\,\delta_I\notin U$ for every $t>0$, and $d(f-t\,\delta_I,f)=t\to0$; hence every neighborhood of $f$ contains points outside $U$;
(ii) every neighborhood of $f$ meets infinitely many distinct chambers, namely all $uC$ with $u\in W_I$.
No local finiteness is claimed at such a point $f$, or at the boundary of $U$ in general.

**(5) The vertex.** $0\in U^\circ$ if and only if $W$ is finite.
items.strategy:
**Finite-parabolic lemma.** Assume $W_I$ finite and $f\in C$ with $S(f)=I$; put $V_I:=\operatorname{span}\{e_s:s\in I\}$ ([[def-linear-subspace]], [[def-linear-combination-and-span]]). First, $\rho(u)$ preserves $V_I$ and $\rho(u)^{-1}e_s-e_s\in V_I$ for all $u\in W_I$ and $s\in S$: for a generator $t\in I$ one has $r_te_s-e_s=-2B(e_s,e_t)e_t\in V_I$ ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] (3)) and $r_t(V_I)\subseteq V_I$, and the claim follows by induction on a word in the generators. On $V_I^*$ consider the dual action $(u\cdot\varphi)(v):=\varphi(\rho(u)^{-1}v)$ for $v\in V_I$. Choose a positive definite form $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_0$ on $V_I^*$ (for instance the sum of products of coordinates in the basis $\varphi\mapsto(\varphi(e_s))_{s\in I}$; [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]], [[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]]) and average it over the finite group $W_I$:
$$\langle\varphi,\psi\rangle:=\frac1{|W_I|}\sum_{u\in W_I}\langle u\cdot\varphi,u\cdot\psi\rangle_0 .$$
The result is again positive definite and symmetric ([[def-finite-cardinality]]) and is $W_I$-invariant, so every $u\in W_I$ acts on $V_I^*$ by isometries of $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$. The action of $t\in I$ is an involution with fixed hyperplane $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_t)=0\}$: $(t\cdot\varphi)(e_t)=-\varphi(e_t)$ and $t\cdot\varphi=\varphi$ precisely when $\varphi$ vanishes on $(\rho(t)-\mathrm{id})V_I=\mathbb Re_t$. Hence $t$ acts as the orthogonal reflection in that hyperplane, and if $n_t\in V_I^*$ represents the functional $\varphi\mapsto\varphi(e_t)$ under $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$, then $t\cdot n_t=-n_t$ and $t\cdot\varphi=\varphi-2(\varphi(e_t)/\|n_t\|^2)n_t$ for all $\varphi$: indeed $\langle\psi,t\cdot n_t\rangle=(t\cdot\psi)(e_t)=-\psi(e_t)=-\langle\psi,n_t\rangle$ for all $\psi$, and $n_t\perp\{\varphi:\varphi(e_t)=0\}$. Let $\gamma:=\sum_{s\in I}\varphi_s$ where $\varphi_s(v)$ is the coefficient of $e_s$, so $\gamma(e_s)=1$ for every $s\in I$. Now let $\varphi\in V_I^*$ and choose $u\in W_I$ maximizing $\langle u\cdot\varphi,\gamma\rangle$ (a maximum over the finite set of real numbers $\{\langle u\cdot\varphi,\gamma\rangle:u\in W_I\}$). If $(u\cdot\varphi)(e_t)<0$ for some $t\in I$, then
$$\langle t\cdot(u\cdot\varphi),\gamma\rangle=\langle u\cdot\varphi,\gamma\rangle-2\frac{(u\cdot\varphi)(e_t)}{\|n_t\|^2}\gamma(e_t)>\langle u\cdot\varphi,\gamma\rangle,$$
contradicting maximality; so $(u\cdot\varphi)(e_s)\ge0$ for all $s\in I$.
**Covering a neighborhood of $f$.** Apply the lemma to $\varphi:=g|_{V_I}$ for $g=f+h\in V^*$: it gives $u\in W_I$ with $(u\cdot(g|_{V_I}))(e_s)\ge0$ for $s\in I$, and $(u\cdot(g|_{V_I}))(e_s)=g(\rho(u)^{-1}e_s)=(u\cdot g)(e_s)$ because $\rho(u)^{-1}e_s\in V_I$. For $s\notin I$ write $\rho(u)^{-1}e_s=e_s+v_u$ with $v_u\in V_I$; then $(u\cdot g)(e_s)=f(e_s)+f(v_u)+(g-f)(e_s)+(g-f)(v_u)=f(e_s)+(g-f)(e_s)+(g-f)(v_u)$, since $f$ vanishes on $V_I$. With $\delta:=\min_{s\notin I}f(e_s)>0$ (if $I=S$ there is nothing to check) and $M:=\max\{\|v_u\|_1:u\in W_I,\ s\notin I\}<\infty$ (finitely many pairs), any $g$ with $\|g-f\|_\infty<\varepsilon:=\delta/(1+M)$ therefore has $(u\cdot g)(e_s)>0$ for all $s\notin I$ and $\ge0$ for $s\in I$, i.e. $u\cdot g\in C$ and $g\in u^{-1}C\subseteq U$. So the whole ball of radius $\varepsilon$ about $f$ lies in $U$, proving $f\in U^\circ$. This is the finite case of (1), and it is exactly the gluing of the finitely many incident chamber sectors into a neighborhood.
**Local finiteness.** Keep $\varepsilon$ as above. If a chamber $vC$ meets the ball at a point $g$, then $g\in uC$ for some $u\in W_I$ by the covering, and $g\in vC$; applying the collision theorem [[thm-cg-dual-chamber-intersections-and-point-stabilizers]] (3) to the pair $(u^{-1}\cdot g,v^{-1}\cdot g)$ and the element $u^{-1}v$ gives $u^{-1}v\in W_{S(u^{-1}\cdot g)}$. For $s\notin I$ we have $(u^{-1}\cdot g)(e_s)=g(\rho(u)e_s)=f(e_s)+(g-f)(e_s)+(g-f)(v'_u)>0$ with $v'_u:=\rho(u)e_s-e_s\in V_I$ and $\|g-f\|_\infty<\varepsilon$; hence $S(u^{-1}\cdot g)\subseteq I$ and $v\in uW_I=W_I$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]). So the chambers meeting the ball are among the finitely many $wuC$, $u\in W_I$. If a wall $W=vH_{e_r}$ meets the ball, take $y\in W$ in the intersection and write $\alpha:=\rho(v)e_r\in\Phi$, so that $W=H_\alpha$; for every $u\in W_I$ one has $H_\alpha\cap uC^\circ=\emptyset$, because $x=u\cdot g$ with $g\in C^\circ$ gives $x(\alpha)=g(\rho(u)^{-1}\alpha)$, the root $\rho(u)^{-1}\alpha$ lies in $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup\Phi_-$, and $g$ is strictly positive on $\Phi_+$ and strictly negative on $\Phi_-$ ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2); the same sign computation as in [[thm-cg-dual-chamber-intersections-and-point-stabilizers]] (2)). By the covering $y\in uC$ for some $u\in W_I$, and $y\notin uC^\circ$ by the previous sentence, so $y$ lies on the boundary of the polyhedral cone $uC=\bigcap_{s\in S}\{f:f(\rho(u)e_s)\ge0\}$, whose boundary is contained in $\bigcup_{s\in S}uH_{e_s}$ (a point where some defining inequality is not strict is a boundary point); hence $y\in uH_{e_s}$ for some $s\in S$. Therefore, applying this to each point of the ball, the nonempty open subset $H_\alpha\cap\{g:d(f,g)<\varepsilon\}$ of the hyperplane $H_\alpha$ is covered by the finitely many intersections $H_\alpha\cap uH_{e_s}$ ($u\in W_I$, $s\in S$), each of which is either all of $H_\alpha$ or a proper affine subspace, and a finite union of proper affine subspaces has empty interior; so $H_\alpha=uH_{e_s}$ for some $u\in W_I$, $s\in S$, and $W$ is one of the finitely many walls $wuH_{e_s}$ of the chambers $wuC$, $u\in W_I$. This proves (3) for $f_0\in C$; for general $f=w\cdot f_0$, apply (i)-(iii) to the ball $B(f_0,\varepsilon)$ and transport along the linear isomorphism $w$: chambers and walls map to chambers and walls, and $w\cdot B(f_0,\varepsilon)$ contains a ball about $f$ (the coordinate bound of [[def-cg-tits-cone-and-fundamental-chamber]] (3)). For a compact $K\subseteq U^\circ$ cover it by finitely many such balls using compactness ([[def-metric-compactness]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-metric-topology]]) and note that a finite union of sets each meeting finitely many chambers or walls meets only finitely many.
**Infinite-parabolic case, (4)(i) and the converse of (1).** Let $f\in C$ and $I=S(f)$ with $W_I$ infinite. Since $S$ is finite, if the length were bounded by $N$ on $W_I$ then $W_I$ would be contained in the image of the finitely many words of length $\le N$ in $S$, hence finite ([[def-finite-cardinality]]); so there are $u\in W_I$ of arbitrarily large length. Every element of $W_I$ has a reduced expression with letters in $I$: writing it as a product of elements of $I$ and repeatedly deleting two letters ([[thm-hh-coxeter-exchange-deletion-and-faithfulness]] (3)) produces a reduced expression whose letters still lie in $I$. For such a reduced expression the suffix formula of [[thm-cg-root-inversion-formulas-and-strong-exchange]] (2) exhibits every element of $N(u)$ as $\rho(v)^{-1}e_s$ with $v\in W_I$, $s\in I$; since $V_I$ is $W_I$-invariant, $N(u)\subseteq\Phi_+\cap V_I$. As $|N(u)|=\ell(u)$ is unbounded, $\Phi_+\cap V_I$ is infinite. Let $\delta_I:=\sum_{s\in I}f_s$ with $f_s$ the dual basis functionals ([[def-dual-family-associated-to-a-basis]], [[thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension]]) and put $g_t:=f-t\,\delta_I$ for $t>0$. Every $\alpha\in\Phi_+\cap V_I$ is a nonnegative combination $\sum_{s\in I}c_se_s$ ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2) puts $\alpha\in V_+\setminus\{0\}$ and $\alpha\in V_I$ forces the outside coefficients to vanish, [[def-linear-combination-and-span]]), so $f(\alpha)=\sum_sc_sf(e_s)=0$ and $\delta_I(\alpha)=\sum_sc_s>0$; hence $g_t(\alpha)=-t\,\delta_I(\alpha)<0$. Thus $\operatorname{Neg}(g_t)$ is infinite and $g_t\notin U$ by [[thm-cg-tits-cone-finite-negativity-and-convexity]] (1). Since $d(g_t,f)=t$ (the difference is supported on $I$ with value $-t$), every neighborhood of $f$ contains points outside $U$, so $f\notin U^\circ$; this is the reverse direction of (1) and clause (4)(i). For (4)(ii): for every $u\in W_I$ the chamber $uC$ contains $f$, because $u\in W_{S(f)}$ fixes $f$ ([[thm-cg-dual-chamber-intersections-and-point-stabilizers]] (4)); distinct $u$ give distinct chambers, since $uC=u'C$ forces $u'^{-1}u$ to preserve $C^\circ$ and the collision theorem (3) of that item gives $u=u'$; and $W_I$ is infinite, so every open set containing $f$ meets all of these chambers.
**(2)** If $f\in U^\circ$ then $f=w\cdot g$ with $g\in C$, and $g\in U^\circ$ because $U^\circ$ is $W$-invariant: $w\cdot U=U$ and $w$ is a linear isomorphism, so $w$ maps a small ball inside $U$ onto a neighborhood of $wf$ still inside $U$. By (1), $W_{S(g)}$ is finite, so $g\in C^f$ and $f\in w\cdot C^f$; conversely every point of $w\cdot C^f$ lies in $U^\circ$ by (1) and $W$-invariance. The identification $C^f=\{f\in C:W_{S(f)}\ \text{finite}\}$ is the definition of the faces $C_I$ ([[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]] (2)).
**(5)** Apply (1) to $f=0$, whose zero set is $S(0)=S$: $0\in U^\circ$ if and only if $W_S=W$ is finite. No Choice is used: the averaging is over the finite group $W_I$, the maximum is over a finite set, and the perturbation is explicit.

items.title: The Tits cone of infinite dihedral type: interior, boundary, and stabilizers
items.statement:
Let $S=\{s,t\}$ with $m(s,t)=\infty$, so that $B(e_s,e_t)=-1$ ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] (2)), and let $W$ be the infinite dihedral group with generators $s,t$ and length $\ell$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]); let $V=\mathbb R^S$, and let $C$, $C^\circ$, the chambers $wC$, the Tits cone $U$, its interior $U^\circ$ and $\operatorname{Neg}(f)$ be as in [[def-cg-tits-cone-and-fundamental-chamber]]. Write a functional as the pair $(x_s,x_t):=(f(e_s),f(e_t))$ and put
$$\Delta(f):=f(e_s+e_t)=x_s+x_t .$$
Then:

**(i) Dual action and invariance of $\Delta$.** The generators act by
$$s:(x_s,x_t)\mapsto(-x_s,\ 2x_s+x_t),\qquad t:(x_s,x_t)\mapsto(x_s+2x_t,\ -x_t),$$
and $\Delta(w\cdot f)=\Delta(f)$ for every $w\in W$.

**(ii) The chambers.** $C$ is the closed positive quadrant; with $u:=st$ one has
$$u^k:(x_s,x_t)\mapsto(x_s-2k\,\Delta(f),\ x_t+2k\,\Delta(f)),\qquad (u^ks):(x_s,x_t)\mapsto(-(x_s+2k\,\Delta(f)),\ x_t+2x_s+2k\,\Delta(f)),$$
for every $k\in\mathbb Z$, and the chambers of the system are the translates $u^kC$ and $u^ksC$ of the quadrant; on each affine line $\{\Delta=\text{const}>0\}$ their traces are unit intervals in the normalized coordinate $a=x_s/\Delta$.

**(iii) The Tits cone, its interior and its boundary.**
$$U=\{f:\Delta(f)>0\}\cup\{0\},\qquad U^\circ=\{f:\Delta(f)>0\},\qquad \overline U=\{f:\Delta(f)\ge0\},$$
and the topological boundary of $U$ is the line $\{f:\Delta(f)=0\}$, of which $U$ contains exactly the point $0$. In particular $U$ is neither open nor closed, and the nonzero boundary points do not lie in $U$.

**(iv) Sample membership tests.** $f=(1,-1)$ and $f'=(-1,0)$ satisfy $\operatorname{Neg}(f)\supseteq\{e_t+ku:k\ge0\}$ and $\operatorname{Neg}(f')\supseteq\{e_s+ku:k\ge0\}$ (with $u=e_s+e_t$), so both sets are infinite and $f,f'\notin U$ by the criterion of [[thm-cg-tits-cone-finite-negativity-and-convexity]] (1); on the other hand $s\cdot(-1,3)=(1,1)\in C$, so $(-1,3)\in U$.

**(v) Stabilizers.** $\operatorname{Stab}_W(0)=W$; $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=\langle st\rangle$ for every $f$ with $\Delta(f)=0$ and $f\ne0$; $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=\{1\}$ for $f\in C^\circ$ and $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=\{1,s\}$ or $\{1,t\}$ for the points of the two open walls of $C$; consequently every point of $U\setminus\{0\}$ has stabilizer of order at most $2$. The outside point $f'=(-1,0)$ has $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f')=\{1,t\}$.

items.title: Chamber faces and their stabilizers in $A_2$
items.statement:
Let $S=\{s,t\}$ with $m(s,t)=3$, so that $c=\cos(\pi/3)=\tfrac12$ and $B(e_s,e_t)=-\tfrac12$ (the value of $c$ is derived in Verification step 1.1 from [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]] and [[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]]; the form is [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]]), let $W$ be the Coxeter group of type $A_2=I_2(3)$ with length $\ell$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), and let $C$, the faces $C_I$, the chambers $wC$, the Tits cone $U$ and its interior $U^\circ$ be as in [[def-cg-tits-cone-and-fundamental-chamber]]. Write $f=(x_s,x_t)$ and $u:=st$. Then:

**(i) The six sectors.** The generators act on $V^*$ by
$$s:(x_s,x_t)\mapsto(-x_s,\ x_s+x_t),\qquad t:(x_s,x_t)\mapsto(x_s+x_t,\ -x_t).$$
The three root lines $H_{e_s}=\{x_s=0\}$, $H_{e_t}=\{x_t=0\}$ and $H_{e_s+e_t}=\{x_s+x_t=0\}$ cut the plane into six closed sectors; these are exactly the six chambers $wC$ ($w\in W$), and $W$ acts simply transitively on them, so $|W|=6$.

**(ii) Wall stabilizers.** For $f=(0,1)$ one has $S(f)=\{s\}$ and
$$\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=W_{\{s\}}=\{1,s\};$$
every point of the open face $C_{\{s\}}=\{x_s=0,\ x_t>0\}$ has stabilizer $\{1,s\}$, and symmetrically every point of $C_{\{t\}}=\{x_t=0,\ x_s>0\}$ has stabilizer $\{1,t\}$.

**(iii) Interior and vertex stabilizers.** For $f=(1,1)\in C^\circ$ one has $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=\{1\}$, and $\operatorname{Stab}_W(0)=W$, of order $6$.

**(iv) An orbit and the intersection rule.** $W\cdot(0,1)=\{(0,1),(1,-1),(-1,0)\}$, of cardinality $3=|W|/|\operatorname{Stab}_W(0,1)|$, and its unique point in $C$ is $(0,1)$; for the reflection $s$ one has $sC\cap C=\{f\in C:x_s=0\}=\{x_s=0,\ x_t\ge0\}$.

**(v) The whole plane is the Tits cone.** $U=U^\circ=V^*$.

**(ii)** $f=(0,1)$ lies in $C$ with $f(e_s)=0$, $f(e_t)=1$, so $S(f)=\{s\}$ and [[thm-cg-dual-chamber-intersections-and-point-stabilizers]] (4) gives $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=W_{\{s\}}=\{1,s\}$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]); the remaining points of the open face $C_{\{s\}}$ are exactly the functionals $(0,x_t)$ with $x_t>0$, all with the same zero set $\{s\}$, so the same formula applies; the claim for $C_{\{t\}}$ is symmetric.
**(iii)** $(1,1)\in C^\circ$ has $S(f)=\emptyset$, so $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=W_\emptyset=\{1\}$; and $0$ has $S(0)=S$, so $\operatorname{Stab}_W(0)=W_S=W$, of order $6$ by (i).
**(iv)** Using $s(0,1)=(0,1)$ ($x_s=0$), $t(0,1)=(1,-1)$, $st(0,1)=s(1,-1)=(-1,0)$, $ts(0,1)=t(0,1)=(1,-1)$, $sts(0,1)=s(1,-1)=(-1,0)$ and $tst(0,1)=t(-1,0)=(-1,0)$, the orbit is $\{(0,1),(1,-1),(-1,0)\}$ of size $3\cdot2=6$ counted with the stabilizer from (ii), and only $(0,1)$ has both coordinates $\ge0$, so it is the unique point of the orbit in $C$; this is the collision theorem ([[thm-cg-dual-chamber-intersections-and-point-stabilizers]] (3)). The intersection rule of that item (5) with $w=s$, together with $s\in W_T\iff s\in T$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]), gives $sC\cap C=\overline C_{\{s\}}\cup\overline C_{\{s,t\}}=\{x_s=0,x_t\ge0\}$.
**(v)** Every standard parabolic of the finite group $W$ is finite, so every point of $C$ satisfies $W_{S(f)}$ finite and the interior criterion [[thm-cg-tits-cone-interior-and-local-finiteness]] (1) gives $C\subseteq U^\circ$. Since $U^\circ$ is $W$-invariant and the six chambers cover $V^*$ by (i), $V^*=\bigcup_wwC\subseteq U^\circ\subseteq U\subseteq V^*$, so all three are equal. No Choice is used.

items.title: A point outside the Tits cone with infinite stabilizer
items.statement:
Let $S=\{s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4\}$ with $m(s_1,s_2)=m(s_3,s_4)=\infty$, $m(s_i,s_j)=2$ whenever one of $s_i,s_j$ lies in $\{s_1,s_2\}$ and the other in $\{s_3,s_4\}$, and $m(s_i,s_i)=1$; thus $W=W_1\times W_2$ with $W_1=\langle s_1,s_2\rangle$ and $W_2=\langle s_3,s_4\rangle$ two infinite dihedral groups ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]). Write $f=(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$ for a functional, put $\Delta_1:=x_1+x_2$ and $\Delta_2:=x_3+x_4$, and let $U$ be the Tits cone of $(W,S)$ ([[def-cg-tits-cone-and-fundamental-chamber]]). Then:

**(i) Block decomposition.** $B$ is block diagonal with blocks $\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$ on $\{e_{s_1},e_{s_2}\}$ and on $\{e_{s_3},e_{s_4}\}$ and zero cross terms, each generator acts nontrivially only on its own block, the dual action is componentwise, and
$$C=C_1\times C_2,\qquad U=U_1\times U_2,$$
where $C_i$, $U_i$ are the chamber and the Tits cone of the $i$-th infinite dihedral factor.

**(ii) The vector.** By [[ex-cg-tits-cone-of-infinite-dihedral-type]] (iii), $U_1=\{f_1:\Delta_1(f_1)>0\}\cup\{0\}$. The functional
$$f=(-1,\ 0,\ 1,\ -1)$$
has $\Delta_1(f)=-1<0$, hence $f_1\notin U_1$ and $f\notin U$.

**(iii) Infinite stabilizer.** $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=\{1,s_2\}\times\langle s_3s_4\rangle$: the first factor is the order-two subgroup fixing the line $x_2=0$ pointwise, the second is infinite cyclic. Hence $f$ is a vector outside the Tits cone whose stabilizer is infinite, so it is not a finite parabolic subgroup of $W$; this shows that an arbitrary vector outside the Tits cone need not have a finite parabolic stabilizer. For contrast, in the rank-two example [[ex-cg-tits-cone-of-infinite-dihedral-type]] the infinite stabilizer $\langle st\rangle$ occurs exactly on the boundary line $\Delta=0$ with the origin removed, which lies outside $U$ but in its closure, and every point with $\Delta\neq0$ has stabilizer of order at most $2$: no $u^k$ with $k\neq0$ fixes it, and $u^ks\cdot f=f$ reduces to the single equation $x_s=-k\Delta$, which determines at most one $k$. Here moreover $\Delta_1(f_1)=-1<0$, so $f$ also lies outside the closure $\overline U=\overline{U_1}\times\overline{U_2}=\{f:\Delta_1(f)\ge0,\ \Delta_2(f)\ge0\}$ of the Tits cone, and the infinite stabilizer is carried by a point strictly outside the closed cone.
items.strategy:
**(i)** For cross pairs the Coxeter entry is $2$, so $B(e_i,e_j)=-\cos(\pi/2)=0$ ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]]), and the two diagonal blocks are the rank-two forms with entry $-1$; hence $B$ is block diagonal. For a generator $s$ in the first block and an element $e_j$ of the second, the reflection formula $r_se_j=e_j-2B(e_j,e_s)e_s=e_j$ shows that $\rho(s)$ fixes the second block pointwise and similarly in the other direction; so $\rho(w_1,w_2)=\rho_1(w_1)\oplus\rho_2(w_2)$, the dual action is componentwise, $C=\{f:x_1,x_2\ge0\}\times\{f:x_3,x_4\ge0\}=C_1\times C_2$, and $U=\bigcup_{(w_1,w_2)}(w_1C_1\times w_2C_2)=U_1\times U_2$ ([[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]], [[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]]).
**(ii)** This is the substitution of the first factor into the description of the infinite dihedral Tits cone in [[ex-cg-tits-cone-of-infinite-dihedral-type]] (iii); membership in the product is componentwise by (i).
**(iii)** An element $(w_1,w_2)$ fixes $f$ if and only if $w_1$ fixes $f_1=(-1,0)$ and $w_2$ fixes $f_2=(1,-1)$, so $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=\operatorname{Stab}_{W_1}(f_1)\times\operatorname{Stab}_{W_2}(f_2)$. For the first factor, with $(s,t)=(s_1,s_2)$ in the rank-two formulas of [[ex-cg-tits-cone-of-infinite-dihedral-type]] (i), $s_2$ acts on $V_1^*$ by $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto(x_1+2x_2,\ -x_2)$ and $s_1$ by $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto(-x_1,\ 2x_1+x_2)$, so $s_2$ fixes the line $x_2=0$ pointwise, hence $f_1$; writing $u_1:=s_1s_2$ one has $u_1^k\cdot x=x+2k\Delta_1(x)(-1,1)$ for the same computation as in [[ex-cg-tits-cone-of-infinite-dihedral-type]] (ii), so $u_1^k\cdot f_1=f_1$ only for $k=0$, while $u_1^ks_1\cdot f_1=(1+2k,-2-2k)$ equals $f_1$ only for $k=-1$, which is the element $u_1^{-1}s_1=s_2$; since $W_1=\{u_1^k\}\cup\{u_1^ks_1\}$, this gives $\operatorname{Stab}_{W_1}(f_1)=\{1,s_2\}$. For the second factor, $f_2$ has $\Delta_2(f_2)=0$ and $f_2\ne0$, so $\operatorname{Stab}_{W_2}(f_2)=\langle s_3s_4\rangle$ by [[ex-cg-tits-cone-of-infinite-dihedral-type]] (v), an infinite cyclic subgroup since $s_3s_4$ has infinite order ([[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] (3)(iv)). Therefore $\operatorname{Stab}_W(f)=\{1,s_2\}\times\langle s_3s_4\rangle$ is infinite; an element $(1,(s_3s_4)^k)$ with $k\ne0$ already lies in it, and every finite parabolic subgroup of $W$ has finite order, so the stabilizer is not a finite parabolic. No Choice is used.
